description: Change of use from Class C3 (dwellinghouse) to Class C2 (for up to 2 children).
decision_conditions: The proposed change of use from a C3 dwellinghouse to a C2 children's home would result in the loss of an existing self-contained family dwelling. Whilst the proposed use would provide a form of specialist accommodation and the submitted Written Statement of Local Need is noted, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the loss of the existing family dwelling would be justified in the wider public interest or that this particular property would be suitable for the proposed use. The proposal would therefore conflict with the objective of safeguarding existing housing stock and would fail to demonstrate compliance with the policy requirements for residential care accommodation, contrary to Policies DMH 1 and DMH 8 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policies H8, H9 and H12 of the London Plan (2021), and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

The applicant has failed to demonstrate that the proposed 24-hour staffed C2 children's home, involving up to two children, daytime and overnight staff, staff handovers, manager attendance and associated professional and visitor movements, would operate without causing undue noise, disturbance and general activity harmful to neighbouring occupiers. In the absence of a sufficiently detailed, site-specific and enforceable management framework, and in the absence of any noise assessment, acoustic report, sound insulation details or other mitigation measures, the proposal would fail to safeguard neighbouring residential amenity, contrary to Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policies D3, D13 and D14 of the London Plan (2021), and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

In the absence of a submitted transport appraisal (including parking surveys) and travel plan demonstrating that for the proposed level of occupancy, the low level of on-plot parking would not lead to measurable and undue displaced on-street parking to the detriment of parking capacity and safety on the local public highway, contrary to Local Plan: Part 2 Development Plan (2020) Policies DMT 1, DMT 2 & DMT 6 and Policy T4 and T6 of the London Plan (2021)."

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from the  Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, as well as offering a full pre-application advice service.
